title: Internship or summer course
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and an academic advisor.

lines.t: I came in last month to register for the summer statistics course, but something's come up.
Good news or bad news?
Good, I think. A marketing firm downtown offered me a paid internship for June and July. The trouble is, it overlaps completely with the course.
Well, statistics is required for your major, so you can't skip it, but it's also offered in the fall. Would taking it then push anything else back?
Not really. I'd just have five courses instead of four that semester.
Five is a heavy load, but you managed it last spring without much trouble. Honestly, an offer like that doesn't come along every summer.
That's what I was hoping you'd say. I'll withdraw from the summer course today and email the firm to accept.

questions.prompt: What does the advisor imply about the internship?
options: It will count toward his statistics requirement.
It will make his fall schedule impossible.
It is an opportunity the student should not miss.
It is less valuable than a summer course.
optionNotes: He still has to take statistics.
She says he managed five courses before.
questions.explanation: 'An offer like that doesn't come along every summer' = it's a rare chance; take it.
questions.evidence: an offer like that doesn't come along every summer

questions.prompt: What will the student probably do next?
options: Drop the summer course and accept the job
Ask the firm to change the internship dates
Register for four courses in the fall
Take the statistics course online this summer
questions.explanation: He will withdraw from the course and accept the internship.
questions.evidence: I'll withdraw from the summer course today and email the firm to accept.

title: Swapping a volunteer shift
context: Listen to a conversation between two students.

lines.t: Sam, you volunteer at the food bank on Saturdays, right? Any chance you could swap shifts with me this week?
Depends. Which shift are you on?
Sunday morning, seven to eleven. My cousin's getting married on Sunday, and I only found out the date last week.
Seven in the morning on a Sunday. You really know how to sell it.
I know, I know. I'd owe you one. I could take your next two Saturday shifts as well, if that helps.
Actually, that would help. I've got a big exam coming up in a couple of weeks. Fine, I'll do Sunday. But you'll have to tell the coordinator, not me. She gets annoyed when people swap without asking.
Fair enough. I'll text her right now.

questions.prompt: What does the man imply when he says the woman really knows how to sell it?
options: The woman is very good at persuading people.
The food bank needs volunteers to sell food.
He would prefer to work on Sunday mornings.
The shift she is offering is not very appealing.
optionNotes: This is the literal meaning, but he is being ironic.
Correct: he is being ironic about the early Sunday start.
questions.explanation: Irony: an early Sunday shift is hard to 'sell', so he means it does not sound attractive.
questions.evidence: You really know how to sell it.

questions.prompt: What will the woman probably do next?
options: Go to her cousin's wedding on Saturday
Send a message to the coordinator
Start studying for an exam
Ask another student to take the shift
optionNotes: The man agreed to take it.
questions.explanation: The man asks her to tell the coordinator, and she agrees to text her.
questions.evidence: I'll text her right now.

title: Narrowing a thesis topic
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a professor.

lines.t: I've read your proposal, Leah. You want to study the history of urban parks in North America.
Yes. I think it's a fascinating topic.
It is. It's also a topic people have written entire careers about. You've got one semester and forty pages.
So it's too broad.
Let's say it's ambitious. What part of it actually got you interested?
Well, I grew up near a park in Montreal that was built on an old railway yard. I've always wondered how the city decided to do that.
Now that's a thesis. One park, one decision, and probably a stack of city council records nobody's looked at in years. The city archive is the place to start.
I'll go there this week, then. I didn't realize I already had a topic.

questions.prompt: What is the professor's opinion of the original proposal?
options: It is not interesting enough for a thesis.
It covers too much for the time and length available.
Another student has already completed it.
It relies too heavily on city records.
optionNotes: Correct: one semester and forty pages.
Records are part of the new, narrower idea.
questions.explanation: 'Ambitious' is a polite way of saying too broad.
questions.evidence: You've got one semester and forty pages.

questions.prompt: What will the student probably do?
options: Rewrite her proposal about all North American parks
Interview members of the city council
Visit parks in other countries
Look for records at the city archive
optionNotes: Correct: she will go there this week.
questions.explanation: The professor recommends the archive and she agrees to go.
questions.evidence: The city archive is the place to start.

title: A guest on the couch
context: Listen to a conversation between two roommates.

lines.t: Hey, quick question. My friend from high school is visiting next week. Would it be okay if he stayed on our couch for a few nights?
How many is a few?
Four, maybe five. He's really easygoing.
I'm sure he is. It's just that I've got my final project due on the Friday, and I'll be working at the kitchen table most nights.
Right, I didn't think about that. What if we kept the living room quiet after nine, and I took him out for dinner most evenings?
That'd help. And maybe he could leave Thursday instead of Friday? That last night is when I'll really need to concentrate.
I'll ask him to change his ticket. I'm sure he won't mind.

questions.prompt: What is the woman's attitude toward the visit?
options: She will agree if her work is not disturbed.
She refuses to let the guest stay.
She is excited to meet the man's friend.
She does not care because she will be away.
optionNotes: She will be at home working.
questions.explanation: She is worried about her project but accepts once the man offers solutions.
questions.evidence: That'd help. And maybe he could leave Thursday instead of Friday?

questions.prompt: What will the man probably do?
options: Cancel his friend's visit
Help the woman with her project
Ask his friend to leave a day earlier
Book a hotel for his friend
optionNotes: Correct: he will ask him to change his ticket.
questions.explanation: The woman asks if the friend can leave Thursday; he agrees to ask.
questions.evidence: I'll ask him to change his ticket.

title: Broken centrifuge
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a laboratory technician.

lines.t: Hi, the centrifuge in room two oh four is making a grinding noise. I stopped it halfway through my run.
Good call. That one's been acting up all month. I put in a repair request, but the parts are on back order.
So it's out of action until when?
Your guess is as good as mine. Could be next week, could be after the semester.
My samples need to be spun today, or they'll degrade.
There's another centrifuge in the biochemistry lab on the third floor. Strictly speaking, it's reserved for their grad students, but Doctor Abbott's usually reasonable if you ask him directly.
His office is on the third floor too, isn't it?
Right next to the lab. Take your samples with you so you don't have to come back down.

questions.prompt: What does the technician mean when she says the student's guess is as good as hers?
options: She wants the student to guess the cause of the noise.
She expects the repair to be finished next week.
She wants the student to fix the machine himself.
She does not know when the machine will be fixed.
optionNotes: That is only one possibility she mentions.
Correct: it could be next week or after the semester.
questions.explanation: The idiom means 'I have no idea'.
questions.evidence: Your guess is as good as mine.

questions.prompt: What will the student probably do next?
options: Wait for the repair parts to arrive
Go upstairs and ask Doctor Abbott for permission
Use the centrifuge in room two oh four
Submit a repair request
optionNotes: Correct: the technician tells him to take his samples up.
questions.explanation: His samples must be spun today, so he will go to the third floor.
questions.evidence: Take your samples with you so you don't have to come back down.

title: Late-night radio slot
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and the manager of the campus radio station.

lines.t: Hi, I'm interested in hosting a show on the campus radio station. I'd like to do one about local bands.
Great. We do have a slot open, but I should warn you, it's Tuesday from midnight to two.
Midnight? Does anyone actually listen at that hour?
More than you'd think. Night owls, people in the library, a few shift workers. It's not prime time, but nobody gets prime time in their first term. That's how most of our best hosts started.
Hmm. I suppose it would be a good way to practise without much pressure.
Exactly. And if it goes well, you can apply for an evening slot in spring. First, though, you'll need to complete a two-hour training session on the equipment.
Okay, sign me up for the next one.

questions.prompt: What is the woman's first reaction to the time slot?
options: She is pleased because she likes staying up late.
She is angry that another host has a better slot.
She doubts that many people would hear her show.
She thinks it clashes with her library job.
optionNotes: Correct: she asks if anyone listens at midnight.
The library is mentioned only as a place listeners are.
questions.explanation: Her question expresses doubt about the audience.
questions.evidence: Does anyone actually listen at that hour?

questions.prompt: What will the woman probably do next?
options: Attend a training session on the equipment
Apply for an evening slot
Interview local bands
Host her first show this Tuesday
optionNotes: Correct: she asks to sign up for it.
Not stated as a next step.
questions.explanation: Training is required first, and she asks to be signed up.
questions.evidence: sign me up for the next one

title: Interview practice
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a career counselor.

lines.t: So, how did the practice interview feel?
Honestly, I thought I nailed it. I had an answer for everything.
You did, and your answers were well prepared. Maybe a little too well prepared. A couple of them sounded like you'd memorized them word for word.
Well, I sort of did.

The committee will notice. They're not looking for perfect answers. They want to see how you think. When I asked about a time you failed, you described a problem that was really a success in disguise.
I guess I didn't want to look bad.
Everyone does that. Next time, pick a real setback and talk about what you'd do differently. Let's run through that question again on Thursday.
Thursday works. I'll think of a better example before then.

questions.prompt: What is the counselor's main concern about the student's answers?
options: They sound rehearsed rather than natural.
They are too short to impress the committee.
They show he has not prepared enough.
They focus too much on his failures.
optionNotes: He avoided talking about a real failure.
questions.explanation: She says his answers sounded memorized.
questions.evidence: A couple of them sounded like you'd memorized them word for word.

questions.prompt: What does the counselor imply about the student's example of a failure?
options: It was too personal to share.
It happened too long ago.
It was not really a failure.
It was his best answer.
questions.explanation: A 'success in disguise' means the story was actually about a success.
questions.evidence: you described a problem that was really a success in disguise

title: Wrong night at the theater
context: Listen to a conversation between two friends.

lines.t: Callum, I've got some bad news about the play tonight.
Don't tell me it's been cancelled.
No, it's worse, in a way. I booked the tickets for the wrong night. They were for last Thursday.
Ah. Well, that's one way to save an evening.
I'm so sorry. I called the box office, and they won't refund them, but they said there are still a few seats left for tonight at the student price.
How few is a few?
Four, in the back row of the balcony.
The back row of the balcony. I'd better bring my glasses, then. Go on, book them before they go, and this time I'll check the date.

questions.prompt: Why does the man say that's one way to save an evening?
options: He is relieved because he wanted to stay home.
He is reacting to the mistake with humor rather than anger.
He suggests they save money by not going.
He is complaining that the play was cancelled.
optionNotes: He wants to go and asks her to book new seats.
He tells her to book the tickets.
questions.explanation: He jokes about the mistake and then agrees to buy new tickets.
questions.evidence: that's one way to save an evening

questions.prompt: What will the woman probably do next?
options: Ask the box office for a refund again
Exchange the tickets for next Thursday
Go to the play by herself
Buy new tickets for tonight's performance
questions.explanation: He tells her to book the remaining seats.
questions.evidence: book them before they go

title: Field course safety training
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a field course coordinator.

lines.t: Hi, I'm on the list for the geology field course in May, but I just got an email saying I haven't done the safety training.
Let me check. Yes, you missed the session in February. I'm afraid it's not optional. Without it, the insurance won't cover you.
I was at a conference that weekend. Is there another session?
There's one on April the twelfth, but it's already full. What I can do is put you down for the online version. It's longer, about six hours, and you'd have to pass a quiz at the end.
Six hours? That's most of a weekend.
I know it's not what you were hoping for, but it's the only way you're getting on that bus in May.
Fine. Send me the link and I'll do it this weekend.

questions.prompt: Why must the student complete the training?
options: It counts toward his final grade.
The conference organizers require it.
He cannot be insured for the course without it.
He failed the quiz in February.
optionNotes: The conference was why he missed it.
He missed the session; he did not fail.
questions.explanation: The insurance will not cover him without the training.
questions.evidence: Without it, the insurance won't cover you.

questions.prompt: How does the student feel about the online training?
options: He is reluctant but accepts that he must do it.
He prefers it to the in-person session.
He refuses because it takes too long.
He expects to be able to skip the quiz.
optionNotes: He complains that it is long.
questions.explanation: He complains about six hours but agrees: 'Fine'.
questions.evidence: Fine. Send me the link and I'll do it this weekend.

title: Language exchange
context: Listen to a conversation between two students.

lines.t: How's the language exchange going? You were meeting that Spanish student, right?
Pablo, yeah. We meet twice a week. Half an hour in English, half an hour in Spanish.
And? Is your Spanish getting better?
Well, his English certainly is. The trouble is, when we switch to Spanish, I get stuck and we drift back into English after about five minutes.
That happened to me with my Korean partner. What helped was picking a topic in advance and writing down a few phrases beforehand. Then you've got something to fall back on.
That's not a bad idea. We're meeting tomorrow, actually. Maybe I'll suggest we talk about football. At least I know the vocabulary for that.
There you go. Just don't let him rescue you by switching languages.

questions.prompt: What does the man imply when he says his partner's English certainly is getting better?
options: His partner already spoke perfect English.
His partner wants to stop meeting.
They speak more Spanish than English.
The exchange is helping his partner more than him.
optionNotes: The opposite: they drift into English.
Correct: his own Spanish is not improving.
questions.explanation: By stressing the partner's progress, he implies his own Spanish is not improving.
questions.evidence: Well, his English certainly is.

questions.prompt: What will the man probably do at the next meeting?
options: Look for a new language partner
Propose a topic for the conversation
Start learning Korean
Cancel the meeting
optionNotes: The woman had a Korean partner.
questions.explanation: He takes the woman's advice and will suggest football as a topic.
questions.evidence: Maybe I'll suggest we talk about football.
